sonnet.problem: This story card re-tells the exact line ("I make all things new") that card 9 just asked about and revealed. The answer "new" is used again, and the card only recaps before adding a joke.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what "the Beginning and the End" tells John about Him. Revelation 21:6 never says what the title means. The card gives a meaning the text leaves open and cites a verse that doesn't state it.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the exact wording "second death". No earlier card has shown this phrase, so the baker cannot reason it out. They can only guess the words of the line.
sonnet.rule: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Card 12 asked whether the gates are shut at day's end and showed the answer. This story card then tells the same fact again ("Never shut"), so the answer is reused.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for "Life" in "the Lamb's Book of ___". No earlier card has shown this title. The baker can only guess the wording, and the wrong answers (Remembrance, the Covenant) are equally plausible by luck.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
